analysis: The PR only changes docs/threat-model.yaml, adding a comment block at head lines 41-48 (patch hunk @@ -38,6 +38,14 @@). It records an SDK 27.2 Date comparison review: App Attest key-generation budget, enrollment resume, stall restart and key history checks now use timeIntervalSince(_:) instead of >= or <=, because the weak-imported Date operators crash on pre-release macOS 27.2. It states thresholds and results are unchanged, and that release builds refuse binaries importing those symbols via scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py. It is a comment-only change with no schema, ID, asset, boundary, threat or mitigation edits, so no canonical threat definitions (A-018, TB-011, T-053..T-058) are altered. I examined the base text in both units (lines 1-876) and found nothing in the patch that conflicts with the existing availability or authorization statements. The documentation claims about unchanged thresholds and the build-time weak-import check cannot be verified from the supplied evidence, because the code changes and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py are not included. The comment ties the crash to A-018 availability, which is a plausible mapping but not a security regression. No new attack surface or invalidated assumption was identified. A later pass should verify, if code is supplied, that the timeIntervalSince substitutions preserve comparison semantics (boundary equality, NaN/clock skew) in App Attest key-generation budgeting and proof-freshness checks, and that the weak-import check script actually runs in the release pipeline.
